title: Kummer class of a divisor and its $c_1$
statement:
Fix the finite-coefficient setting of [def-pur-conventions], with $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ and arbitrary $n\geq1$. In the separated finite-type $k$-scheme setting of [sk-def-purity-conv], let $T\to B$ be smooth of relative dimension $d$ and let $D\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed subfamily smooth over $B$, of pure codimension one as in [def-pur-frame-class]. Thus $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. There is a canonical Kummer divisor class
$$\operatorname{cl}(D)\in H^2_D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A(1))$$
with supported cohomology as in [def-pur-support-cohomology] and twist as in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. It is the global class constructed from the line bundle $\mathcal O_T(D)$ with its canonical section trivializing it on $T\setminus D$, by the relative torsor Kummer connecting map [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology], followed by the coefficient map on roots prescribed in [def-pur-frame-class]. For every etale neighbourhood $U\to T$ on which $D_U$ has equation $f$, its restriction is
$$\operatorname{cl}(D)|_U=-\partial\kappa(f)\in H^2_{D_U}(U,A(1)).$$
Here the relative construction is read in the Yoneda extension convention of [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary]: its lifting torsor over the supported section one is the frame torsor of $\mathcal O_T(D)$, and its specified frame on $T\setminus D$ maps to zero. In particular it is the negative of the rank-one frame class of [def-pur-frame-class], independently of the equation as in [lem-pur-frame-independence].

The same relative construction defines $\operatorname{cl}(E)$ for any effective Cartier divisor $E$ on $T$, including a sum of smooth divisors. If $D_1,D_2$ are such divisors and $Z=|D_1|\cup|D_2|$, then, after the canonical enlargement-of-support maps,
$$\operatorname{cl}(D_1+D_2)=\operatorname{cl}(D_1)+\operatorname{cl}(D_2)\quad\text{in }H^2_Z(T,A(1)).$$
Here $D_1+D_2$ is defined by the product of the two Cartier ideals, so locally its equation is $f_1f_2$, not the two-element frame $(f_1,f_2)$. Forgetting support sends $\operatorname{cl}(D)$ to $c_1(\mathcal O_T(D))\in H^2(T,A(1))$. Precisely, $c_1(L)$ means the ordinary etale Kummer connecting image of the frame-torsor class of $L$ [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor], at exponent $m=\ell^n$ killing $A$, mapped to the pro-etale twist by the same coefficient morphism as [def-pur-frame-class]. No $\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$-module structure on $\mathbf G_m$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the existing unique normalized Cartier-family construction. Its componentwise SupportedKummerBoundary witnesses determine classOf, and realizes determines homClassOf, so no arbitrary relative-class data is chosen.

The smooth codimension-one Cartier theorem supplies the invertible ideal of i. Apply normalizedCartier_localEquation to its normalized representative for both the singleton frame and boundary descriptions. This is the c_D convention of the current blueprint, the negative of its frame class.

For a product ideal use invertibility of the product, Ideal.mul_le_left and Ideal.mul_le_right, and the universal property of closed immersions to construct hsum and the two inclusion maps. Apply normalizedCartier_sum to the three representatives and their realizes witnesses.

Apply normalizedCartier_forget to the etale representative and its realizes witness. It supplies the ordinary Ext representative, its Hom identity, Chern normalization and compatibility of forgetting support with the same site comparison.

proof_origin.place: Relative class c_D, local Yoneda sign, product-ideal addition and forget-support comparison; implemented using the existing unique family and ordinary Chern normalization

statement_change.what: The positive local-equation formula mixed the signed-cone relativeConnecting convention with the recorded Yoneda/extClass convention. In SupportedKummerBoundary the frame action is smulMor(g) followed by e, tau=g*e, F(tau)=0, and equivariance forces F(e)=-a(g). The local extension is the pushout of localization along 1 to g inverse, so its Kummer Yoneda product is -boundary(kappa(f)), while its ordinary image is +c1(O(D)). For k an algebraic closure of F_2, ell=3, E=Q_3, n=1, U=A1_k and f=t, the boundary has residue 1 in F_3, so it differs from its negative. Both local clauses must be negated; globally negating the class would break the Chern clause.

old_proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates] to $D\hookrightarrow T$ over $B$. The ambient finite-type setting is explicitly that of [sk-def-purity-conv]. Thus $T$ and $D$ are finite type over $k$, hence locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field has just the two ideals $0,k$, so its spectrum is Noetherian). At a point $y\in D$, the coordinate chart gives a regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_b$ in $R=\mathcal O_{T,y}$ defining $\mathcal O_{D,y}$. Each $f_j$ lies in the maximal ideal of its successive quotient and is a nonzerodivisor there. The successive quotients remain Noetherian, since their ideals correspond to ideals of $R$ containing the quotient ideal, and the images of generators generate. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] successively to obtain $\dim R=\dim\mathcal O_{D,y}+b$. The pure-codimension convention in [def-pur-frame-class] says the difference is one, so $b=1$. Thus locally $\mathcal I_D=(f)$ with $f$ a nonzerodivisor; off $D$ the ideal is the unit ideal. This proves that $D$ is Cartier and that one-function frames exist, without presuming regularity of the base. We will construct the global class rather than infer a global cohomology class from equality of local classes.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, lemma-etale-local-structure, applied to the first sentence of the blueprint proof

old_proof.text: For any effective Cartier divisor $E$ put $L_E=\mathcal I_E^\vee$ as in [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. On a chart $\mathcal I_E=(f_a)$ write $e_a=f_a^{-1}$ for the dual basis, and put $s_E=f_ae_a$. On overlaps $e_b=(f_a/f_b)e_a$, so $f_be_b=f_ae_a$: these sections glue. On $W=T\setminus E$ this section is nowhere zero and gives a specified trivialization $\tau_E:\mathcal O_W\simeq L_E|_W$. By [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor], $P_E=\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(\mathcal O_T,L_E)$ is a $\mathbf G_m$-torsor, with the specified section $\tau_E$ on $W$.

source.place: First sentence and final paragraph; canonical section on the complement

old_proof.text: Use [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] for $G=\mathbf G_m$ to obtain $\alpha_E=[(P_E,\tau_E)]\in H^1(T,W;\mathbf G_m)$. Its forgotten-support image is $[P_E]$. This is a specified class, not an arbitrary lift of a Picard class. Replacing $f_a$ by $u_af_a$ changes $e_a$ to $u_a^{-1}e_a$ and leaves $s_E$ unchanged. Thus the pair and its relative class are independent of all local equations.

source.place: First sentence: global well-definedness via a torsor with its specified section

old_proof.text: Put $m=\ell^n$, which is invertible on $T$ and kills $A$ in the conventions and coefficient prescription of [def-pur-frame-class]. Apply [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] and the relative connecting map of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] to form $\beta_E=\delta_{T,W}(\alpha_E)\in H^2(T,W;\mu_m^{\mathrm{et}})$. Its image in ordinary cohomology is $\delta_T([P_E])$, by the relative lemma's compatibility with forgetting support. Only the exact sequence of abelian sheaves is used here, with no tensoring of $\mathbf G_m$ over $\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence; relative connecting construction from the blueprint final paragraph

old_proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-divisor-relative-cone] to $(T,W)$ and the etale root sheaf $\mu_m^{\mathrm{et}}$. It identifies $\beta_E$ with a supported etale class and supplies its canonical comparison with pro-etale relative cohomology. Apply the coefficient morphism $\sigma_T\rho_T:\nu_T^{-1}\mu_m^{\mathrm{et}}\to A(1)_T$ of [def-pur-frame-class] to define $\operatorname{cl}(E)\in H^2_E(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A(1))$. The relative-cone lemma identifies this group with the support-kernel derived group of [def-pur-support-cohomology] and states that these maps commute with forgetting support, etale restriction, the localization boundary and enlargement of support. Thus all those compatibilities hold for this global class at every coefficient index $n\geq1$.

source.place: Support boundary and final paragraph; comparison performed on both terms of the relative cone

old_proof.text: Let $h:U\to T$ be an etale neighbourhood with $E_U=(f)$. The pullback of the pair $(P_E,\tau_E)$ along $h$ is $(P_{E_U},\tau_{E_U})$, since $\mathcal I_E$, its dual and $s_E$ pull back; so by the pullback naturality of the bijection and of the connecting maps in [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology], $\alpha_E$ and $\beta_E$ restrict to $\alpha_{E_U}$ and $\beta_{E_U}$. On $U$ the dual basis $e=f^{-1}$ trivializes $P_E$; its specified section on $U_f$ has coordinate $g=f|_{U_f}\in\mathbf G_m(U_f)$. By [lem-pur-divisor-torsor-boundary-signs] its canonical relative class is represented by $(0,g)$ in the cone $D(a,b)=(da,\operatorname{res}a-db)$ and is $-\partial[g]$. Apply the same lemma's short-exact-sequence assertion to the Kummer sequence of step 4: it gives $\delta_{U,U_f}(\alpha_{E_U})=\partial\delta(g)$, with the positive sign (both sides have representative $(0,-dr)$ for a lift $r$). Step 5 and its boundary-compatible coefficient map then give $\operatorname{cl}(E)|_U=\partial\kappa(f)$. For smooth $E=D$, this is exactly the single-factor frame class of [def-pur-frame-class]; [lem-pur-frame-independence] agrees with the independence already supplied by the global pair construction.

source.place: Clause (a), with explicit relative-cone boundary calculation

old_proof.text: For $E=D_1+D_2$ let $\mathcal I_E=\mathcal I_{D_1}\mathcal I_{D_2}$. On simultaneous Cartier charts $f_1f_2$ is a nonzerodivisor because both factors are, so $E$ is Cartier even when it is not smooth; its complement is $W=T\setminus(|D_1|\cup|D_2|)$. Multiplication identifies the ideal tensor product with the product ideal on these bases, hence $L_E\simeq L_{D_1}\otimes L_{D_2}$, carrying $s_E$ to $s_{D_1}\otimes s_{D_2}$. The frame torsor is therefore the contracted product by [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor], including its specified section over $W$. To see addition in relative $H^1$ from precisely the stated naturality of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology], take the product torsor for $\mathbf G_m\times\mathbf G_m$ and its pair of sections. The two projections give $(\alpha_{D_1},\alpha_{D_2})$ in relative cohomology, since the two-term restriction cone commutes with finite products. Push out along multiplication $\mathbf G_m\times\mathbf G_m\to\mathbf G_m$: on these additive cohomology groups it is addition, and on torsors it is their contracted product. Thus $\alpha_E=\alpha_{D_1}+\alpha_{D_2}$ in $H^1(T,W;\mathbf G_m)$. For $W\subseteq W_i=T\setminus|D_i|$ the restriction square gives the chain map $(a,b)\mapsto(a,b|_W)$ of signed cones; by the representative $(a,h(s))$ of [lem-pur-divisor-torsor-boundary-signs] it sends $\alpha_{D_i}$ to the class of $(P_{D_i},\tau_{D_i}|_W)$, which is this enlargement of support. On the split cone sequences of the Kummer resolutions it is a morphism of short exact sequences, so it commutes with the relative connecting maps by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality], and with the comparison and coefficient maps by step 5. The connecting and coefficient maps of steps 4-5 are homomorphisms, so their images give the required equality in $H^2_Z(T,A(1))$. This proves global additivity without a local-to-global injectivity claim for $H^2_Z$.

source.place: Clause (b), addition; correcting the source two-function frame to the product equation

old_proof.text: Finally, step 4 gives $\operatorname{forget}(\beta_D)=\delta_T([P_D])$. Step 5 commutes with forgetting support, so $\operatorname{forget}(\operatorname{cl}(D))$ is the ordinary Kummer boundary of the frame-torsor class of $L_D=\mathcal O_T(D)$, followed by exactly the same roots coefficient morphism. This is $c_1(\mathcal O_T(D))$ by the definition in the statement. The torsor interpretation of the line bundle is [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor], and the compatibility of the relative connecting map with forgetting is the explicit last assertion of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology]. The equality holds globally; it is not deduced from restriction of ordinary $H^2$ to trivializing opens.

source.place: Final paragraph: forget-support comparison with the ordinary Kummer connecting class

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $T\to B$ be smooth of relative dimension $n$ and let
$D\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed subfamily, smooth over $B$, of pure
codimension one. The *Kummer class of the divisor $D$* is the
class $\operatorname{cl}(D)\in H^2_D(T,\Lambda(1))$ of
[def-pur-frame-class] of a frame of the ideal of $D$, well
defined by [lem-pur-frame-independence]. Moreover:

1. *(a)* $\operatorname{cl}(D)|_{U}=\partial(\kappa(f))$ in
$H^2_{D\cap U}(U,\Lambda(1))$ for a local equation $f$ of $D$ on an open $U$.
1. *(b)* Forgetting support sends $\operatorname{cl}(D)$ to
$c_1(\mathcal O_T(-D))=-c_1(\mathcal O_T(D))$. Here $\mathcal O_T(-D)$ is
the ideal sheaf of $D$. Equivalently, the class
$c_D\in H^2_D(T,\Lambda(1))$ of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map], built from
$\mathcal O_T(D)$ with its canonical section, is $-\operatorname{cl}(D)$.
1. *(c)* For any two functions $f_1,f_2$ on an open $U$ of $T$, with zero
loci $D_1=V(f_1)$ and $D_2=V(f_2)$ (not necessarily smooth over $B$),

$$
\partial\kappa(f_1f_2)=\partial\kappa(f_1)+\partial\kappa(f_2)
\quad\text{in }H^2_{D_1\cup D_2}(U,\Lambda(1)),
$$

the classes $\partial\kappa(f_i)\in H^2_{D_i}(U,\Lambda(1))$ being mapped
along the extension of supports from $D_i$ to $D_1\cup D_2$. Consequently
$\operatorname{cl}(D_1+D_2)=\operatorname{cl}(D_1)+\operatorname{cl}(D_2)$
whenever $D_1$, $D_2$ and $D_1+D_2$ are all smooth over $B$ of pure
codimension one, so that the three classes are defined.

proof.text:
Use the frame class of [def-pur-frame-class], independent of the local equation by [lem-pur-frame-independence], and the support boundary of [def-pur-support-cohomology] applied to the Kummer datum of [def-pur-affine-line-datum].
(a) is (def. frame class) $\operatorname{cl}(f)=\partial(\kappa(f))$.

For (c), put $W=U\setminus(D_1\cup D_2)$. The Kummer class is the image of a
unit under the connecting map
$H^0(-,\mathbf G_m)\to H^1(-,\mu_{\ell^N})$ of the Kummer sequence of
[def-pur-affine-line-datum], followed by the coefficient extension; both
are group homomorphisms, so $\kappa(f_1f_2)=\kappa(f_1)+\kappa(f_2)$ in
$H^1(W,\Lambda(1))$. The support boundary
$\partial:H^1(W,\Lambda(1))\to H^2_{D_1\cup D_2}(U,\Lambda(1))$ is a
homomorphism, and it is natural for the map of pairs
$(U,D_i)\to(U,D_1\cup D_2)$: the boundary of the restriction of
$\kappa(f_i)$ from $U\setminus D_i$ to $W$ is the extension of supports of
$\partial\kappa(f_i)$, because sections supported on $D_i$ are sections
supported on $D_1\cup D_2$ and the two support sequences of
[def-pur-support-cohomology] form a commutative ladder. Applying $\partial$
to the additivity of $\kappa$ gives (c). If $D_1$, $D_2$ and $D_1+D_2$ are
smooth over $B$ of pure codimension one, then on an open $U$ where
$D_1,D_2$ have local equations $f_1,f_2$, the product $f_1f_2$ is a local
equation of $D_1+D_2$, so by (a) and (c) the global classes
$\operatorname{cl}(D_1+D_2)$ and $\operatorname{cl}(D_1)+\operatorname{cl}(D_2)$
agree on every such $U$; they agree globally because they are glued from
these local classes (the definition of $\operatorname{cl}$ via
[lem-pur-frame-independence]).

For (b) we show $c_D=-\operatorname{cl}(D)$, where
$c_D\in H^2_D(T,\Lambda(1))$ is the class of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map];
since $c_D$ forgets support to $c_1(\mathcal O_T(D))$ and
$c_1(\mathcal O_T(-D))=-c_1(\mathcal O_T(D))$ by
[lem-pur-kummer-additivity], this gives (b). Both classes are global
classes supported on $D$ that are determined by their restrictions to the
members of a cover by opens $U$ on which $D$ has a local equation $f$ (this
is how $\operatorname{cl}(D)$ is defined globally), so it suffices to compare
them on such a $U$. Put $U^\circ=U\setminus D$ and work first with
$\mu_{\ell^N}$-coefficients.

*The relative class.* Let
$\partial_{\mathbf G}:H^0(U^\circ,\mathbf G_m)\to H^1_{D\cap U}(U,\mathbf G_m)$
be the support boundary for $\mathbf G_m$. It sends a unit $g$ on $U^\circ$
to the trivial line bundle together with the trivialization $g$ on $U^\circ$.
Multiplication by $f$ is an isomorphism
$\mathcal O_U(D)=f^{-1}\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal O_U$ carrying the canonical
section $1$ to $f$, so $\partial_{\mathbf G}(f)$ is the relative class of
$\mathcal O_T(D)$ with its canonical trivialization used in
[lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map], and $c_D|_U=\delta(\partial_{\mathbf G}(f))$,
where $\delta$ is the Kummer boundary on cohomology supported on $D\cap U$.
The same relative class is the boundary of $1$ in the divisor extension
$0\to\mathbf G_m\to\mathcal M_D\to i_*\mathbf Z_D\to0$, where
$\mathcal M_D\subset v_*\mathbf G_m$ ($v:T\setminus D\hookrightarrow T$) is
generated by $\mathbf G_m$ and $f^{-1}$ and $f^{-1}\mapsto1$, so that the
lifts of $1$ are the local generators of $\mathcal O_T(D)$; and the sign
is checked directly: if $\mathbf G_m\to I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution and
$\psi:\mathcal M_D\to I^0$ extends its augmentation, the connecting
morphism $i_*\mathbf Z_D\to\mathbf G_m[1]$ sends $1$ to the class of
$-d\psi(f^{-1})\in\Gamma_{D\cap U}(U,I^1)$ (on a horseshoe resolution
$I^\bullet\oplus J^\bullet$ of $\mathcal M_D$ with differential
$(a,b)\mapsto(da+hb,db)$, the connecting morphism is $h$ composed with the
augmentation of $J^\bullet$, and the augmentation $(\psi,\epsilon_J\pi)$ of
$\mathcal M_D$ is a chain map only if $h\epsilon_J\pi=-d\psi$), and
$\psi(f^{-1})$ extends $f^{-1}$ from $U^\circ$, so this class is
$-\partial_{\mathbf G}(f^{-1})=\partial_{\mathbf G}(f)$.

*The two boundaries anticommute.* By (a),
$\operatorname{cl}(D)|_U=\partial(\delta(f))$, with $\delta$ now the Kummer
boundary on $U^\circ$ and $\partial$ the support boundary for $\mu_{\ell^N}$.
Choose a short exact sequence of injective resolutions of the Kummer sequence
and apply sections supported on $D\cap U$, sections on $U$ and sections on
$U^\circ$. This gives a $3\times3$ diagram of complexes with exact rows (the
Kummer direction) and exact columns (the support direction, exact because
injective sheaves are flasque), and $\delta$, $\partial$ are the connecting
maps of its rows and columns. For a $3\times3$ diagram of complexes the two
composite connecting maps from the corner $(3,3)$ to the corner $(1,1)$ are
opposite: lift a cocycle $z$ of the corner $(3,3)$ to $x$ in the centre;
then $dx=b+g$ with $b$ in the corner $(2,1)$ and $g$ in the corner $(1,2)$,
the two composites are the classes of $db$ and $dg$, and
$db+dg=d^2x=0$. Applied to $z=f$,

$$
\operatorname{cl}(D)|_U=\partial\delta(f)=-\delta\partial_{\mathbf G}(f)=-c_D|_U.
$$

Hence $c_D=-\operatorname{cl}(D)$ with $\mu_{\ell^N}$-coefficients, and
with $\Lambda(1)$-coefficients after the coefficient extension of
[def-pur-affine-line-datum], which commutes with both boundaries.
